title: Check your agent's task briefs for gaps before it starts
summary: A developer found 90% of 61 fix requests traced to his own vague work orders, then had Claude check each order first, catching about 60% of gaps per $0.07 run.
agent_role: Claude writes work orders and a cheaper model, MiMo, codes them in separate branches; an automatic reviewer sends work back. A new Claude 'falsifier' pass reads each order and lists ways it could go wrong; the human edits the order before handoff.
outcome: Author reports 55 of 61 must-fix items came from silent or vague orders; one falsifier run caught 56–60% of those gaps, about 71% across two runs, at about $0.07 each.
what_they_did: Zhuojun Li has Claude plan code changes as written work orders and a cheaper model, MiMo, write the code. After rework rose, he sorted 61 fix requests from 10 orders by cause. He then added a step where Claude reads each order, quotes weak lines, and gives a concrete input that breaks it, before the worker starts.
how_it_went: He says 90% of rework items came from orders that were silent or unclear. Running the check twice caught 71% of those gaps. Three of four new orders then passed review first time, which he says is too small a sample to judge.
worth_knowing: Two runs of the check disagreed a lot, so he runs it twice. He also moved a 'never print passwords' rule from the prompt into a tool block after it was broken four times.
prompt: Before I hand this task brief to my coding agent, act as a critic. Read [work order file] and look at the code in [repo path], but don't write any code. Return up to seven ranked problems. For each, quote the line of the brief that causes it, or say 'not mentioned'. Give a concrete input or situation that would break the result. Name the section of the brief where the fix belongs. I'll update the brief myself.

curation.rationale: A data-driven follow-up that sorts real rework items, finds most came from vague briefs, and adds a cheap pre-handoff check with costs and hit rates. Small sample, but honest and practical.
